SYNTHETIC TEST WORDING - NOT AN INSURER'S DOCUMENT
Written for ClaimClear's policy-kb tests. It imitates the numbered structure of a standard
Arogya Sanjeevani policy wording, in our own words. Do not cite it as policy wording.

Aarohan General Insurance Ltd. - Arogya Sanjeevani Policy (synthetic)
UIN: SYNHLIP00000V000000

1. PREAMBLE
This policy is a contract between the insured person and the company. The schedule, the proposal and these terms together form the contract.

2. OPERATIVE CLAUSE
The company will pay reasonable and customary medical expenses for hospitalisation of an insured person during the policy period, subject to the terms, conditions, limits and exclusions in this wording.

3. DEFINITIONS
3.1 Accident means a sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, visible and violent means.
3.2 Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement under which the insured person bears a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount.
3.3 Day care treatment means medical treatment or a surgical procedure done in less than 24 hours because of technological advancement, which would otherwise need hospitalisation of more than 24 hours.
3.4 Hospital means an institution established for in-patient care and day care treatment, registered with the local authorities, with qualified nursing staff round the clock and a fully equipped operation theatre.
3.5 ICU charges means the amount charged by a hospital for each day of stay in an intensive care unit, including bed charges, monitoring devices and critical care nursing.
3.6 Pre-existing disease means any condition, ailment, injury or disease diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 36 months before the first policy issued by the company.
3.7 Reasonable and customary charges means charges for services that are consistent with the prevailing charges in the geographical area for identical or similar services.
3.8 Room rent means the amount charged by a hospital for occupying a bed, on a per day basis, together with associated medical expenses.
3.9 Associated medical expenses means expenses that vary with the room category, such as nursing charges, surgeon and consultant fees, anaesthetist fees and operation theatre charges.

4. COVERAGE
4.1 Hospitalisation
The company will pay medical expenses for in-patient care of at least 24 consecutive hours, including:
i. Room rent, boarding and nursing expenses up to 2% of the sum insured per day, subject to a maximum of Rs. 5,000 per day.
ii. Intensive care unit charges up to 5% of the sum insured per day, subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,000 per day.
iii. Surgeon, anaesthetist, consultant and specialist fees, operation theatre charges, medicines, drugs, diagnostics, blood, oxygen and surgical appliances.
4.2 AYUSH treatment
The company will pay medical expenses for in-patient care under Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy in an AYUSH hospital, up to the sum insured.
4.3 Cataract treatment
The company will pay expenses for cataract treatment up to 25% of the sum insured or Rs. 40,000, whichever is lower, per each eye in one policy period.
4.4 Pre-hospitalisation expenses
Medical expenses incurred in the 30 days immediately before the date of admission are payable, if the hospitalisation claim is admissible.
4.5 Post-hospitalisation expenses
Medical expenses incurred in the 60 days immediately after discharge are payable, if the hospitalisation claim is admissible.
4.6 Modern treatment methods
Listed modern treatments such as robotic surgeries and stem cell therapy are covered up to 50% of the sum insured during the policy period.

5. PROPORTIONATE DEDUCTION
5.1 Associated medical expenses
If the insured person occupies a room category with rent above the eligible limit, the associated medical expenses payable are reduced in the same proportion as the eligible room rent bears to the actual room rent.
5.2 Items not reduced
The proportionate deduction does not apply to pharmacy, consumables, implants, medical devices and diagnostics, to ICU charges, or to any expense the hospital does not charge differently by room category.

6. CO-PAYMENT
Each admissible claim is subject to a co-payment of 5% of the admissible claim amount, applied after all other deductions.

7. WAITING PERIODS AND EXCLUSIONS
7.1 Pre-existing diseases (Code Excl01)
Expenses for treatment of a pre-existing disease are excluded until 36 months of continuous coverage have elapsed since the date of inception of the first policy with the company.
7.2 Specified disease or procedure waiting period (Code Excl02)
Expenses for the listed conditions are excluded until 24 months of continuous coverage have elapsed since the first policy, and for joint replacement until 36 months. The list includes cataract, hernia, hydrocele, piles, fistula, sinusitis, gall bladder stones, kidney stones, gout and rheumatism, and diseases of the joints.
7.3 First 30 days waiting period (Code Excl03)
Expenses for any illness contracted within 30 days from the first policy commencement date are excluded, except claims arising from an accident.
7.4 Investigation and evaluation (Code Excl04)
Expenses incurred primarily for diagnostics and evaluation purposes, not followed by active treatment during the hospitalisation, are excluded.
7.5 Continuity of cover
Waiting periods are counted from the inception of the first policy and continue on renewal without a break. A renewal does not restart any waiting period.

8. NON-PAYABLE ITEMS
Items listed in Annexure I, such as gloves, masks, caps, admission kits and registration charges, are not payable.

9. CLAIM PROCEDURE
9.1 Notification of claim
The insured person shall notify the company within 24 hours of an emergency admission, or 48 hours before a planned admission.
9.2 Documents for reimbursement
The claim form, hospital bill with itemised break-up, discharge summary, investigation reports, payment receipts and prescriptions shall be submitted within 30 days of discharge.
9.3 Settlement of claim
The company shall settle or reject a claim within 30 days of receiving the last necessary document. If the company delays payment, it shall pay interest at 2% above the bank rate.
9.4 Itemised breakdown
On request, the company shall give the insured person an itemised statement of every amount deducted from the claim, with the reason and the policy clause relied on.

10. GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL
10.1 Grievance officer
An insured person with a grievance may write to the company's grievance officer. The company shall acknowledge it and respond within 14 days.
10.2 Insurance Ombudsman
If the grievance is not resolved within 30 days, or the insured person is not satisfied with the response, they may approach the Insurance Ombudsman within one year of the company's final reply.

ANNEXURE I - LIST OF NON-PAYABLE ITEMS
Gloves, masks, caps, shoe covers, admission kits, registration charges, attendant charges, diet charges for attendants, toiletries, and documentation charges.
